gen-fs-oswald-fs-public-sans: Confident and tightly knit, Oswald stacks its lines like a row of upright planks. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, which gives the page a sturdier, more trustworthy footing.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-ranade: Oswald packs its rows of text tight and tall, a display face with a low-key, confident stroke variation. Ranade loosens everything up, with stroke ends far apart and a slight, rubbery shift in weight.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-spline-sans: Oswald leads with tightly knit, confident lines. Spline Sans, a plain sans, draws its horizontals exactly as heavy as its verticals, and wide gaps between curve ends and stems keep the text approachable below the heading.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-armata: Strong, then spacious. Oswald packs its rows tight and moderate in height, while Armata, a plain sans, spreads out with wide terminal gaps and a lowercase filling most of the letter height; shrink the heading and that tension would fade.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-cardo: Tight, tall and sure of itself. Oswald is best at punching out confident display lines, and Cardo, a serif, is best at literary text, with softly varied strokes and thins that never turn spindly.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-cascadia-code: Confident and compact, Oswald holds its lines close. Cascadia Code, a sans with a wire-like monoline skeleton and a taller lowercase, stands apart with spacing you can't miss and smooth, unobstructed curves.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-chakra-petch: Chakra Petch reads as a plain sans with cupped, rounded letters and one steady stroke width. Oswald is best at confident, tightly knit display lines, and the body font is best at keeping that line thickness constant.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-domine: Oswald's tightly knit rows give it a strong, confident look all its own. And Domine, a text serif with compact ascenders and a breathing space inside every curve, handles the reading with a modest dip in its thin strokes.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-epunda-slab: Oswald sets a confident, tightly knit display line over a moderate lowercase. And Epunda Slab, a serif, contrasts it with tall rounded forms and a visibly gaping c, which is the pair's most striking quality.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru glows like neon tubing, with stroke ends set far apart. Under Oswald's confident, tightly knit heading, this plain sans keeps its stroke widths put from stem to curve, so paragraphs would move along smoothly.
